body: Ten cases here started at or near an IPO. Low-multiple PSU or out-of-favour listings: HAL (Mar 2018 at ~14x) first fell −56% in two years, then reached ~9x the issue price at its 2024 peak; Cochin Shipyard (2017 issue ≈₹216 adjusted) ~13x at peak; Mazagon (2020, issue ≈₹72.5 adjusted, ~7x P/E) ~48x at peak; CDSL (2017, ≈₹74.5) ~26x; BSE (2017, ≈₹90 adjusted) ~47x. Fairly priced private leaders: Polycab (2019, ~20–27x) ~19x; Dixon (2017, ~60x) ~52x, only because EPS rose ~10x on the PLI scheme. Boom-market listings: Kaynes (2022, ~100x) ~13x at peak and now −62% from it; Waaree (2024, 84x on first close) and Premier (214x) tripled EPS but are below their first close (1.6–1.8x the issue price). Pattern: what matters at listing is the P/E, not the story. Government or out-of-favour IPOs at low multiples left both engines available; hot-sector IPOs at 80x+ left only EPS, and those stocks fell 40–60% at the first stumble. Also, IPO buyers of winners often waited 1–3 years through a −50% drawdown (HAL, Dixon, CDSL). Issue prices here are from general knowledge and should be re-checked (unverified).

data.boom_ipos: Kaynes, Waaree, Premier: -37% to -62% from peak
data.low_pe_ipos: HAL, Cochin, Mazagon, CDSL, BSE: 9-48x at peak

title: IPO entry: PSU listings at <15x became 8–48x; hot-market listings at 80–200x went to −50–60%

body: Worksheet v1 on three practice companies (test material, no verdict). With cost of equity 12.5%, terminal growth 5% and terminal ROIC 25-30%, the terminal value is worth ~11-15x NOPAT ((1 - tg/ROIC)/(r - tg) ~ 0.8/0.075 ~ 10.7x at 25% ROIC), so DCF-consistent P/Es at year 5 came out at 12-17x while VMM and Cummins trade at 48-52x: probability-weighted DCF values were -65% and -69% vs price. The informative outputs were (1) the reverse DCF: the price needs ~30% revenue CAGR for 10 years at today's margins, and the path needs reinvestment above 100% of NOPAT at the assumed ROIIC (feasibility flag); (2) the IRR the price offers if the base case happens: 7-8% vs a 12.5% hurdle; (3) the exit-multiple gap: every Indian scenario's stated exit P/E (25-50) was 2-3x its DCF-consistent P/E, i.e., the 5-year return depends on the market continuing to pay high multiples. Rule: for Indian high-P/E names, report implied IRR and the exit-multiple gap, never 'DCF value -65%' as a target; the decision gate uses the 5-year multiple vs the index hurdle. Caveat: the base-rate class used alongside (2020-25 NSE survivors, x3 44%) is bull- and survivor-biased.
title: At India CoE 12-13% a DCF calls almost every 40-50x compounder 60-70% overvalued; read the implied IRR and the exit-multiple gap instead
